title: Unified Inference - Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (Q3 2027)
author: Daniel Kim
summary: This document describes the Unified Inference product surface for Q3 2027: the product overview, prioritized requirements (PRD), high-level design specs, roadmap and themes for the next three quarters, pricing and packaging recommendations, and release notes for the v24 release. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success teams preparing go-to-market and onboarding materials.
background: Redwood's Unified Inference consolidates the platform runtime, model catalog, and routing controls to provide a single developer API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes. The v24 initiative focuses on predictable unit economics, improved developer ergonomics for function/tool calling, and enterprise readiness for regulated customers.
goals: Deliver predictable per-token unit economics for common web-app workloads (>=20% cost improvement for high-cache hit workloads vs v22)
Expose feature-complete function and tool-calling primitives in SDKs and Console with deterministic streaming semantics
Provide standardized observability and quality checks: per-route token-cost breakdowns, prompt-level regressions, and rollout controls for model/quantization variants
Ship Dedicated & Private onboarding checklist to reduce customer setup time to <7 days for standard configurations
non_goals: Major changes to the serving runtime kernel selection logic (out of scope for v24; incremental perf tuning only)
Replacing existing RBAC model for Private deployments (policy changes deferred)
success_metrics: Average cost-per-1k tokens for chat workloads reduced by 15% vs v22 baseline
P95 generation latency for 512-token sessions <= 220ms on our Hosted tier for small/medium models
Customer onboarding time for Dedicated standard config <= 7 days
NPS improvement for new integrations (target +6 points in pilot customers)
product_requirements: The following high-level requirements capture the product and customer expectations for v24. Each requirement is prioritized and mapped to an owner and acceptance criteria in the release backlog.
functional_requirements: API: Stable /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints with explicit support for function/tool calls and structured JSON output
Streaming: Deterministic chunking semantics and client-side SDK helpers for reconnect/resume
Model Variants: Support named variant groups (e.g., 'high-qa', 'low-cost-quantized') with automated fallback routing
Cost Controls: Route-level batching, per-route cache policies, and token price estimates surfaced in Console
Dedicated: Reserved capacity contracts with autoscaling policies and SLA configuration options
Private: Hardened control-plane connector and KMS/HSM integration guide for air-gapped deployments
Observability: Token-level breakdowns, per-route P50/P95 latency, and prompt set regression alerts
non_functional_requirements: SLOs: Hosted P99 generation latency < 800ms for 1024-token sessions (small models), uptime >= 99.95%
Security: All customer data in transit encrypted (TLS 1.3) and at rest encrypted with customer-managed KMS for Private customers
Scalability: Autoscaler support to 500 qps per Dedicated pool with graceful degradation policies
Operational: Runbooks for partial-failure scenarios and SLA breach playbooks documented in eng-sre
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end API tests passing for function/tool calling, streaming, and resume semantics
Benchmarks demonstrating cost improvements on representative workloads (chat, embeddings, reranking)
Pilot with at least two customers (one mid-market SaaS, one enterprise) with onboarding checklist completed
Console pages and SDKs updated, docs published, and sales enablement pack delivered
design_overview: v24 is an incremental product release that stitches together several subsystems: the routing layer (policy engine), serving runtime (quantization and batching), and Console/SDK surface for developer ergonomics. Design focuses on clear separation between routing policies (cost/latency/region) and runtime capabilities (model variants, quantization profiles).
architecture_diagram_text: Logical components: API Gateway -> Policy Router -> Model Catalog -> Runtime Pools (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) -> Observability / Metrics Store. Fallbacks: Policy Router will fall back to compatible variant groups when primary variant is saturated or unhealthy.
key_design_choices: Policy-first routing: policies are stored in the control plane and evaluated per-request to enable cost-aware fallbacks
Named variant groups to simplify compatibility checks across model families and quantization profiles
Streaming semantics standardized across SDKs to avoid partial-output regressions during reconnections
security_and_compliance_notes: Private customers will receive a hardened connector with KMS/HSM recommendations and an audit-log schema. Compliance evidence artifacts (SOC2 items, encryption proofs) are referenced in security-and-compliance. Any customer-specific exceptions must be coordinated with Legal and Security.

pricing_summary: v24 introduces a simplified pricing model that separates compute (per-token generation) and capacity (Dedicated reservation) with explicit discounts for high cache-hit workloads and committed usage.
pricing_tiers: Hosted - Developer (pay-as-you-go): $0.015 per 1k prompt tokens / $0.030 per 1k generated tokens; embeddings $0.0008 per vector
Hosted - Production (volume discounts): base price 10% lower after $1M monthly spend; high-cache workloads receive up to 20% effective discount via cache credits
Dedicated - Reserved Capacity: Monthly reservation starting at $9,000/month per 8x GPU pool; overage billed at 50% of on-demand token price
Private - Enterprise License: Platform fee + per-GPU servicing fee; pricing is contractual (contact Sales)
Add-ons: Extended observability retention (30/90/365 days), Compliance package (SOC2 + annual review), Premium SLAs
pricing_rationale: Separate compute and capacity reduces surprise bills for customers that need predictable throughput. Cache credits encourage prefix and KV caching patterns that reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs.
packaging_notes: Bundled deliverables include: Console and SDK updates, Dedicated reservation templates, Private deployment connector package, onboarding checklist, and security attestation packet. Sales enablement will include price calculator and migration worksheet.
launch_readiness: Docs: API reference, migration guide, and console walkthrough published

Sales: Enablement training and price calculator available
Support: Tiered runbooks and known-issues matrix uploaded to support portal
release_notes: v24 (2027-06-30) - GA release. Highlights: function/tool calling standardized across SDKs; streaming resume semantics implemented; named model variant groups and cost-aware routing; Dedicated reservation templates and autoscaling policies; Console updates with per-route token cost breakdowns and regression alerts. See the detailed items below.
release_note_items: Feature: Deterministic streaming and resume semantics in Python/JS SDKs
Feature: Named variant groups + automatic cost-aware fallback routing
Feature: Console — per-route token cost estimates and historical token-cost charts
Feature: Dedicated — reservation templates + configurable autoscaling policies
Improvement: Default batching heuristics tuned to reduce tail latency for 512-token sessions
Security: Private connector supports customer-managed KMS and audit-log export
Bugfix: Fixed edge-case for KV cache invalidation leading to stale prefix returns
rollout_plan: Phase 2 (GA): Public rollout for Hosted and Dedicated standard configs (2027-06-30)
Phase 3 (Enterprise): Private deployments and contract-based pricing (starting 2027-07-15)
Rollback criteria: >3 customer-facing incidents in 7 days or P95 latency regression >20% vs baseline
migration_and_onboarding_notes: Migration guide included in docs: mapping old model IDs to variant groups, recommended cache policies per workload, Dedicated reservation sizing template, and step-by-step Private connector install. For high-volume customers, recommend a staged migration with canaries and A/B testing.
open_risks: Risk: Quantization regressions for certain instruction-tuned models — mitigations: per-variant QA harness and automatic rollback
Risk: Misconfigured autoscaling leading to capacity thrash — mitigations: conservative default scaling and improved monitoring
Risk: Customers misunderstanding pricing tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Hosted — mitigations: improved pricing calculator and Sales training
